correctness.rationale: For one prime p^a, equality forces a=2. At >=2 distinct primes, if all a_p<=2 then sum p^{a_p}< (sum p)^2, so some exponent >=3. Omega<=5 leaves precisely (3,1,1), (3,2), (3,1), (4,1) (after ordering p<q) with the larger prime exponent <=2, since q^3>(p+q)^2. Each is eliminated by the displayed modular factorizations: t(t-1)=0 mod p in the three-prime case, q=p(p-1)/2 in (3,2), and p^{a-2}=(kp-1)^2+k for (a,1). The explicit 144=2^4 3^2 has B=25=(2+3)^2 and Omega=6. Direct independent enumeration n<=100000 agrees; proof handles all n.
